newsitem.title: ITALY: Parliament approves contested Italian tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Parliament approves contested Italian tax reform.

text.p: The lower house of parliament on Wednesday approved the controversial framework for a wide-reaching fiscal reform contained in the Italian government's 1997 budget.

Opposition parties are boycotting the budget debate to protest over the tax changes. The government has not yet given full details of the reform but asked for proxy powers to work out the small print without further recourse to parliament.
The lower house approved the outline for the reform along with the request for proxy powers and then suspended debate on the budget until 1630 GMT.
The tax reforms were contained in article 63 of the budget. There are some 70 articles in the main body of the budget, which the lower house is scheduled to approve by Thursday.
The Italian budget is divided into three sections:
-- The so-called connected draft law, which contains all the actual articles.
-- The finanziaria, which contains the overall spending plans for the various sectors, giving a broad outline of where state money will go next year.
-- The state budget, which outlines the budgets for each of the various government ministries.
After parliament has approved the connected draft law it will vote on the remaining two sections. This is not expected to take much time.
After the budget has been approved by the lower house it has to go to the Senate (upper house) for ratification. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
